description: Aging infrastructure economic transition fiscal constraint and entrenched inequality shape long-term urban viability.
Rapid population growth and infrastructure deficits create intense demand for inclusive service expansion.
Flood risk sea-level exposure insurance pressure and stormwater stress shape coastal urban futures.
High connectivity and global capital flows create both operational capacity and digital governance risk.
Real estate capital platform systems and speculative growth produce displacement and public value leakage.
Public investment housing stability climate adaptation and governance capacity reinforce resilience.
Informal housing transit labor and mutual aid systems fill formal service gaps under rapid change.
Fiscal stress fragmented authority maintenance neglect and declining trust amplify urban fragility.
